main_text.p: sionem: nouum autem spiritualia bona, & cœlestem patriam, potissimum respiciat.
{4}. Iam quum Paulus diserte dicat, Fœdus nouum præstantioribus promissis esse sanctum. Heb. 6. 8. negat idem esse cum priore illo, quod antiquandum erat.

7. Porrò, quando idem, fide venisse, Christo Iesu in carne exhibito, verè ostendit. Gal. 3. 13. certè negat eam fuisse veteris Testamenti temporibus. Vnde liquet, pluri-mùm, fidei (quæ pastiones maximè commendat) respectu, inter vetus & nouū Testamentum interesse?

8. Quum etiam Patres, nec eadem, quæ nos, Sacramenta: nec etiam eandem Sacramenti diem (Christo videlicet nondum in carne exhibito) habuerint: inter illorum & nostrum fœdus manifesta differentia, esse videtur.
9. Remissionem autem peccatorum, quū sic noui Testaméti propriam esse aiat Pau-lus: vt veteri eam deroget, Heb. 10. 18. ea sa-ne ratione, nō eandem esse pastionem per spicuè ostendit.
10. Denique vetus testamentum, vt ὡς παλαιὸν, seu oppositum, à nouo plané antiquatum esse, idè solidissimè euincit, Hebr. 8. 7. vsq; ad finem.
Vt autem, quid tibi, vir reuerende & eruditissime

page.notes: Marginal reference "Heb. 6.8." and "Gal. 3.13." appear inline in the text as printed; the Greek word in §10 is partly illegible at this resolution and is transcribed as best read. The number "4" at the start of §4 is a printed paragraph number, with the first letter partly obscured. The footer "O 4" is a signature mark. Catchword: "ditissime" appears to be a catchword rather than running text; it is kept as printed. Several Latin words are blurred; the page is damaged by show-through from the reverse, which has been ignored.
